clue.text: Bureaucrat, one who numbers runners?

definitions.meaning: a fussy official obsessed with costs and figures
a whimsical reading: someone who counts runner beans, a common British garden vegetable

explanation.surface: A sports official, perhaps, keeping count of the competitors in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' looks like athletes, but it means runner beans, so a counter of beans.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a petty official or accountant preoccupied with figures and budgets.

clue.text: Male went first prepared for action

parts.note: a buck is a male deer or rabbit
to go first is to lead; past tense led

explanation.surface: A man took the lead, ready for whatever came next.
explanation.walkthrough: To buckle (to, or down) is to set to work, hence prepared for action.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckling on armour or buckling down means getting ready and setting to work in earnest.

clue.text: South America's greatest current asset

parts.note: current means a flowing river, not present-day; the continent's mightiest river

explanation.surface: Reads like an economist naming the most valuable resource South America has today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' seems to mean present-day, but it is a stream of water: the continent's largest river.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent's largest river by volume is the great waterway flowing through Brazil to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Smart Alec's brother? One is irritatingly knowledgeable

definitions.meaning: a smart Alec has a sibling with a similarly clever-sounding name: two male names, Alec and Dick
a know-all who shows off what they know

explanation.surface: A family of clever-clogs, with one sibling who is a tiresome know-all.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are British colloquial terms for a show-off know-all; one pairs a first name with smart, the other with clever.

clue.text: Unpleasant and somewhat smug lyricist

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A songwriter who is both conceited and disagreeable.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly mood or scene is a nasty, disagreeable one, so the word works as a synonym here.

clue.text: Carefully observe a keen tot exercising

indicators.note: putting the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch closely as an eager toddler runs about doing exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' rearranges A KEEN TOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay careful attention to something and register it is a familiar idiom for observing closely.

clue.text: Pity about TV detective

parts.note: re means concerning or about
Inspector Morse, the Oxford detective of the British television series

explanation.surface: A viewer feels sorry for a television sleuth.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is the hero of a long-running British TV detective series set in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Old and literary use gives the word the sense of compassion, alongside its usual meaning of regret.

clue.text: Mooring charge coming from plant long time afterwards

indicators.note: the long time is placed after the plant in the answer

parts.note: dock is a broad-leaved weed
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A harbour fee arriving long after a factory was built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory, but it is the weed dock.
explanation.definitionFit: Dockage is the fee a vessel pays for berthing at a dock.

clue.text: Deciding to put off digging

parts.note: deter means to discourage or put off
mining is digging for minerals

explanation.surface: Making up one's mind to postpone some excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' looks like postponing; here it means discourage.
explanation.definitionFit: To determine something is to settle or resolve it, so the present participle means resolving.

clue.text: As insane with great energy

parts.note: like can mean in the manner of, as
mad means insane

explanation.surface: Someone crazed and bursting with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a frenzied way is to do it furiously, with tremendous vigour.

clue.text: Those over there accepting blame after main treatment of disease

indicators.note: the first part comes after the sea in the clue's ordering, so the sea goes first in the answer

parts.note: the deep is the sea, the main

indicators.note: they take in blame, holding it within

parts.note: they means those people
a rap, as in taking the rap, is blame or punishment

explanation.surface: People abroad shoulder the blame once a major cure fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the poetic word for the open sea, not 'principal'; 'accepting' is a container signal and 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is radiotherapy using high-energy rays aimed at tissue well below the skin, a medical treatment.

clue.text: Discuss when speech has finished

definitions.meaning: chat or speaking is done, at an end

explanation.surface: An instruction to debate once the address is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a phrasal verb meaning debate, and read literally means chatting is finished.

clue.text: If it is, don't you believe it

definitions.text: If it is, don't you believe it

parts.words: If it is, don't you believe it
parts.note: something that is false should not be believed

explanation.surface: A sceptic's warning about some claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false or inaccurate is just what one should not believe.

clue.text: Measured over half of amount provided I lead occasionally

indicators.note: more than half of the word is kept, its last letters dropped

parts.note: a quantity is an amount
if means provided that

indicators.note: only some of the letters are taken, every other one

explanation.surface: Weighed out more than half a portion, with someone in charge now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over half of' keeps QUANT from QUANTITY; 'occasionally' takes ED, alternate letters of LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To quantify is to express or assess something as an amount, so the past form means gauged.

clue.text: Daughter comes in to be apologetic for something impolite

indicators.note: the letter for daughter enters, sitting inside the regret word

parts.note: to rue is to regret something

explanation.surface: A daughter arrives to apologise for bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' puts D inside RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude and impolite are close synonyms for discourteous behaviour.

clue.text: In tandem arranged fair adaptation

indicators.note: fair is placed in the rearranged letters
the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: just means fair

explanation.surface: A tweak made to a bicycle built for two, set up fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the phrase 'in tandem', but it is the container signal; 'arranged' is the anagram signal, giving ADMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a modification or alteration made to fit, a synonym of adaptation.

clue.text: Old rioter in trouble outside

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: the word is in disarray, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A former troublemaker in difficulty, left out in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' turns RIOTER into TERIOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the outer surface or outward part of something.

clue.text: I name worker accepting poisonous inebriant

indicators.note: the worker takes on the poisonous word, which stands just in front of it

parts.note: toxic means poisonous
a worker ant; ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: Naming a labourer who has taken in something poisonous and intoxicating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' might suggest a container, but the poisonous word simply sits in front of the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a substance, such as alcohol, that makes a person drunk.

clue.text: Practical skill of detective Nicholas shortly going round hospital

indicators.note: the two pieces surround the hospital letter

parts.note: tec is short for detective

indicators.note: the name is cut short, its last letter lost

parts.note: Nick is a familiar form of the name
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A sleuth called Nicholas soon visits a hospital, putting his know-how to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims the last letter of the short name; 'going round' wraps the joined pieces around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Technic is a less common form of technique, the practical method or know-how of an art.

clue.text: Land lies in ruins

indicators.note: the word is wrecked, its letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A territory left devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' rearranges LIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a piece of land surrounded by water; the poetic short form.

clue.text: Type of home visit: rent rises during this

indicators.note: the reversed piece falls within the visit word

parts.note: a stay is a visit

indicators.note: in a down clue the word goes up, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to rent out

explanation.surface: A holiday stay somewhere grand, where the rent goes up the whole time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses in a down clue, giving TEL; 'during' is the container signal. A stately home is a grand British country house, often open to visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the grand country houses, so it names a type of home.

clue.text: Handles fruit

definitions.meaning: paw is to handle roughly, and a doubled paw suggests repeated handling
the tropical fruit also called papaya

explanation.surface: Someone fingering produce at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: A playful double definition: paw twice suggests pawing, i.e. handling.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya, a tropical fruit, is also known by this reduplicated name.

clue.text: Felt like scratching

parts.note: having an irritation of the skin, or a restless urge to do something

explanation.surface: Someone in the mood to pull out of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratching' suggests withdrawing from a race, but it is the urge to scratch skin, and also an eager longing.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both a skin irritation and an impatient longing to act.

clue.text: Greeting old country, it's to do with mountains

definitions.note: a singular name for a whole range of peaks

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Malaya was the former name of the Malaysian peninsula

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a former nation that is all about its peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: The name refers to the great Asian range of peaks including Everest.

clue.text: Specialised food shop, one third of it

indicators.note: only the first third of the full twelve-letter word is kept

parts.note: refers back to the specialised food shop just named, by its full name

explanation.surface: A specialist grocer, given just a third of the description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one third of' keeps the first four letters of DELICATESSEN, its usual short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form is the everyday name for a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and fine foods.

clue.text: Real information on one taken in by a Parisian?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the numeral is held inside the French word

parts.note: une is French for a
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Authentic details about someone deceived by a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Parisian' means the word for 'a' as said in Paris; 'taken in by' is the container signal. Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and real both mean authentic, not fake.

clue.text: Lack of reverence from naughty child that is teary on vacation

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Disrespect from a little rascal who is tearful about the holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties TEARY to TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiety is a want of piety or respect towards God or sacred things.

clue.text: How overenthusiastic stretcher case was transported?

definitions.meaning: excited to the point of losing self-control
an injured person on a stretcher is literally borne off

explanation.surface: Asking how a patient on a stretcher was moved, while hinting at someone too excited.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means swept up by emotion; literally it says lifted and taken off.
